title: Induced path distance on a round unit sphere
edition: Self-contained geometric supplement, 2026-11-16; expanded exposition of the exact 2026-11-09 contract
attribution: Original exposition of a classical round-sphere distance formula; no claim of novelty or attribution to a primary textbook theorem.

units.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with \(\dim E=n+1\), where \(n\ge1\), and let \(S=\{z\in E:\|z\|=1\}\). For the literal inclusion \(\iota:S\to E\), give a tangent vector \(v\) at \(z\) the length \(\|D\iota_z(v)\|_E\). Define \(d_S(x,y)\) as the infimum of the lengths of all \(C^1\) paths on the closed unit interval from \(x\) to \(y\), using this induced speed. For every \(x,y\in S\), including coincident and antipodal endpoints, this distance is the angle \(\arccos\langle x,y\rangle\).
assumptions: \(E\) has a real inner product and finite dimension \(n+1\); \(n\) is a positive natural number. The rank equality selects the standard \(n\)-dimensional sphere manifold model. Positive sphere dimension is used to find a tangent direction for antipodal endpoints.
\(S\) is the actual unit sphere in \(E\), and both endpoints are arbitrary points of \(S\). No distinctness or nonantipodality hypothesis is imposed.

The tangent length is induced by the actual differential of the inclusion into \(E\). It is not a default chart-coordinate norm. The sphere retains its inherited chord metric as a topological subtype; no metric instance is replaced.

The infimum ranges over \(C^1\) paths on the closed unit interval with the prescribed endpoints. The formal distance is an extended nonnegative real and path length is a lower integral; the equality proves that the value is finite.

All differentiability and integrability of the constructed paths, and the scalar norm law needed by the path-length API, are proved internally. There is no supplied path, geodesic, derivative bound, length estimate, or additional measure structure among the theorem hypotheses.

definitions.meaning: Actual unit sphere and literal inclusion.
Ambient norm after the actual inclusion differential; no default chart metric.
Length of an endpoint-constrained C1 path on the closed unit interval.
Extended nonnegative infimum; the theorem proves it is finite.

proof.title: Identify the speed through the actual inclusion
proof.text: For an admissible sphere path \(\gamma\), write \(f=\iota\circ\gamma\). The manifold chain rule identifies its ambient velocity with the image of the path velocity under the inclusion differential. Thus the induced tangent speed is exactly the ambient speed. Within-interval derivatives give the same value at every interior point; endpoints have zero length measure.

proof.title: Control the derivative of the scalar inner product
proof.text: From the unit-norm constraint \(\|f(t)\|=1\), differentiation gives \(\langle f,f'\rangle=0\). Put \(c(t)=\langle x,f(t)\rangle\). Its derivative is the pairing of \(f'(t)\) with \(x-c(t)f(t)\). Expanding the squared norm of that vector and applying Cauchy–Schwarz gives the required estimate. No unit-speed parametrization of the arbitrary path is assumed.

proof.title: Regularize the angle and pass to the endpoint
proof.text: Fix \(0<a<1\). The function \(\arccos(a c(t))\) stays away from the derivative singularities at \(\pm1\). Its derivative is bounded above by the speed, because the displayed square-root ratio is at most one. Continuity makes the derivative integrable on the compact interval. Integrate the bound, then pass to \(a=1\) by continuity, using \(c(0)=1\).

proof.title: Choose a great-circle plane, including the degenerate cases
proof.text: Set \(\theta=\arccos\langle x,y\rangle\) and \(r=y-\langle x,y\rangle x\). The residual is orthogonal to \(x\), with norm \(\sin\theta\). If it is nonzero, normalize it. If it vanishes, choose a unit vector in the orthogonal complement, which has positive dimension. The same endpoint identity holds both for coincident and antipodal points.

proof.title: Build an admissible arc of the required length
proof.text: The ambient curve \(f_*(t)=\cos t\,x+\sin t\,u\) lies on the sphere and lifts smoothly to it. Its ambient speed is one. It connects \(x\) to \(y\) on \([0,\theta]\), so its length is \(\theta\), including the zero-length case. The path-length comparison handles reparametrization to the unit interval. Linearity of the inclusion differential supplies the local scalar norm law used by that comparison.

proof.title: Compare the lower integral with every admissible path
proof.text: For any admissible path, continuous ambient within-interval speed is integrable. The induced lower integral equals the nonnegative embedding of its ordinary speed integral, since the two integrands agree on the interval interior. The lower angle bound therefore applies to every admissible path. Together with the explicit upper arc, this gives equality for the length infimum.

boundary: This identifies the induced length distance of a positive-dimensional unit sphere. It leaves the ambient chord metric unchanged; for antipodal points these two distances are \(2\) and \(\pi\).
The condition \(n>0\) is essential for arbitrary endpoint pairs: the two-point sphere has no continuous internal path between its two distinct points.

It supplies no global Riemannian bundle instance, general manifold geodesic-existence theorem, transport estimate, stochastic result, or textbook chapter completion. Spherical transport is a possible consumer of the distance identity.
